title: fancy-sign data mode: fsig-data-1, the canonical byte form of the data a data-mode envelope signs

contract.summary: fsig-data-1 is sign/chain canonical JSON (SPEC section 1) with one change: a non-integral number prints as ECMAScript Number::toString (RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.3) instead of being refused. The top level must be an object ({} allowed). An integral number prints as an integer (12.0 is 12, -0.0 is 0) and is refused beyond 2^53 - 1. Keys sort by UTF-8 byte order; slash, non-ASCII and U+2028/U+2029 are raw; a lone surrogate is refused. data_sha256 is the lowercase hex sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes, data_bytes their length. Inputs are JSON TEXT, so the decoder is part of what is tested. See SPEC.md section 6.

functions.canonical: canonical({text}) -> {canonical, sha256, bytes} | {error: "refused"}. `text` is the data as JSON text; a runtime must decode it keeping {} and [] (and {"0": x} and [x]) apart.

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are particle-academy/fancy-sign's own output (FancySign\Data\CanonicalDocument), written by fancy-sign-php/tests/Conformance/Export.php from the thirteen CC-fancy-0052 plan vectors. Before the package existed the same thirteen hashes were computed by two independent design sketches (Node and PHP); the package reproduces all of them.

notes: tests/discrimination-sign.test.ts holds a faithful Node reading of SPEC section 6.1 and the mutants a port would plausibly be: PHP's own float form, floats refused, UTF-16 key order, an assoc decode, -0 printed as -0, float noise rounded, unsafe integers accepted, escaped slashes or U+2028, and {} refused. Each mutant names the exact rows that catch it.
